policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Neuter τὸ πλοῦτος and masculine τὸν πλοῦτον differ only in gender; both give ASV 'the riches of their liberality'. The mapped note is a greek_gloss on ἁπλότης ('Greek singleness'), not on this word's form, so nothing in the English distinguishes the readings.
παρὰ δύναμιν and ὑπὲρ δύναμιν both mean 'beyond their power', which is exactly what ASV prints; the English preposition-free rendering 'beyond' cannot separate the two.

ASV reads 'in your love to us', i.e. ὑμῶν ... ἐν ἡμῖν, and its mapped textual_variant note assigns the other direction to the margin: 'Some ancient authorities read our love to you' = ἡμῶν ἐν ὑμῖν. Text and note together select r01.

ASV's 'according as a man hath' supplies a subject that English requires for the impersonal ἐὰν ἔχῃ just as readily as it renders an explicit τις; no note is mapped here, so the addition is not distinguished.
ASV's 'and ye distressed' is the ordinary coordination of the second clause and would stand with or without δέ after ὑμῖν; nothing in the English marks the connective.

ASV renders the participle as a present, 'who putteth the same earnest care ... into the heart of Titus'. The aorist δόντι would give 'who put'; the present tense in the English answers to present διδόντι.

ASV expands the phrase to 'in the matter of this grace', a periphrasis that neither σύν nor ἐν excludes — 'with us' already renders συνέκδημος ἡμῶν, so the surviving 'in the matter of' does not fix the preposition governing τῇ χάριτι.

ASV prints 'to the glory of the Lord' with no 'himself'. Leaving an intensive αὐτοῦ unrendered beside τοῦ κυρίου is a rendering choice rather than a textual signal, and no note is mapped to the unit, so the omission does not settle it.

ASV has a finite clause with the connective: 'for we take thought for things honorable'. That is προνοοῦμεν γάρ; the RP participle προνοούμενοι carries no γάρ and would continue the preceding sentence rather than open one.

ASV renders an imperative, 'Show ye therefore unto them', which is ἐνδείξασθε; the participle ἐνδεικνύμενοι would give 'showing'. The mapped note is classed alternative_rendering and concerns only the placement of 'unto them', so it does not bear on the verb.
